newsitem.title: JAMAICA: SOCCER-JAMAICA SHOCK HONDURAS AND MEXICO CRUISE HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JAMAICA SHOCK HONDURAS AND MEXICO CRUISE HOME.

text.p: Jamaica shocked their more experienced opponents Honduras, beating them 3-0 in a World Cup qualifying match on Sunday, while Mexico won by the same score away to St Vincent in their first match in the tournament.

Jamaica, who have strong traditions in cricket and athletics but no real prowess in soccer, were faster and more powerful than the Central Americans in the CONCACAF qualifying tournament semifinal stage group three match.

Honduras, who qualified automatically for the group and have an appearance in the 1982 World Cup to their credit, fell behind in the 15th minute when striker Walter Boyd scored with a powerful shot on the turn.

The Jamaicans, who came through a preliminary round tie against Surinam, dominated the first half with Hector Wright and Theodore Whitmore inspiring the team in midfield and were rewarded when Whitmore scored in the 42nd minute.
Boyd scored again eight minutes into the second half, finishing off a chance created by Onandi Lowe after which Jamaica, coached by Brazilian Rene Simoes, let up.
Mexico, who also qualified automatically for the group, had a comfortable start to their campaign with striker Ricardo Pelaez scoring twice.

The match was played at the Arnos Vale cricket stadium in Kingstown, the St Vincent capital. St Vincent qualified for the group by winning preliminary ties against Puerto Rico and St. Kitts and Nevis.
Pelaez opened the scoring with a 14th minute header but Mexico's play in the first half was often scrappy, giving the mainly amateur home team a few chances on the counter-attack.
Mexico asserted their authority better in the second half after bringing on Joaquin del Olmo in midfield and Jose Lundis in attack.
Pelaez put them two ahead in the 48th minute, scoring from a rebound after St. Vincent goalkeeper Melvin Andrews failed to hold a free kick taken by Claudio Suarez.
In the last minute, substitute Damian Alvarez scored with a shot from the edge of the penalty area.
The top two teams qualify for the CONCACAF final qualifying round along with the top two sides in each of the other two semifinal groups.
